verdict.rationale: Homebrew's core is a BSD-2-licensed CLI that installs and runs on the user's own macOS, Linux or WSL machines, even under a non-admin account. Its package sources can also be self-hosted: taps accept any Git URL, and taps can provide their own bottles. A community report says hosting a tap needs a full git server rather than a static CDN; this is a friction point, not a contradiction. Missing for 10: a documented guide to self-hosting the formulae JSON API or bottle infrastructure, simpler static-file tap hosting, and independent hands-on corroboration of a fully self-hosted setup.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: Code is under the BSD 2-clause 'Simplified' License.
Homebrew installs the command-line tools and applications you need across macOS, Linux and WSL.
Homebrew can be installed for a non-admin account.
the two-argument form accepts any URL supported by Git.
This may be useful for taps that wish to provide bottles for their formulae or cater to a non-default HOMEBREW_CELLAR.
